materials.caption:
A new University of California, Berkeley study suggests that artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT are making it easier for students to obtain top grades in university, while also reducing the value of those grades for employers assessing graduates’ abilities.

The research, which analysed more than 500,000 grades across courses before and after ChatGPT’s release, found that classes heavily reliant on writing and coding saw a sharp rise in A grades. 

Professors in these AI-exposed subjects awarded about 30 percent more A’s, while fewer A-minus and B-plus grades were recorded, indicating a shift in grade distributions rather than improved learning outcomes. 

Researchers argue the pattern suggests students may be using generative AI to complete assignments more effectively, particularly in unsupervised, homework-based tasks. This, they say, risks inflating grades without necessarily improving understanding or skill levels. 

The findings raise concerns for employers, who increasingly rely on grade point averages to evaluate graduates. If AI tools are significantly influencing academic performance, grades may become a less reliable indicator of genuine ability in writing, coding and analytical tasks.

Educators are responding by redesigning assessments, increasing in-person examinations and reducing reliance on take-home work to better capture independent student learning.
